_comment: BDH object list (Salesforce-shaped). Keys of selectedFields = BDH column names (case-insensitive lookup). Values = Graph property name, or a _bdh_<name> placeholder when the field is consumed by the searchable content body instead of becoming a Graph property. aclMode: ownerOnly (record owner via identity store; ownerField default OwnerId, ownerEmailField default OwnerEmail), group (fixed Entra group - aclGroupId required), public (everyone except guests; explicit opt-in). sourcePath overrides the object's directory under the BDH root (defaults to objectName). sensitivityDefault floors the CLASSIFICATION label. coarseAclAcknowledged + coarseAclAcknowledgedFor (INTERIM control, see docs/ACL_POSTURE.md): explicit human sign-off that an object's COARSE grant (aclMode group or public) has been reviewed and its over-sharing exposure accepted. BOTH keys are required. coarseAclAcknowledgedFor records WHICH posture was reviewed, verbatim: 'public', or 'group:<aclGroupId>'. Without that binding the sign-off says only that someone signed, never what they signed, so it would survive a later widening (group -> public, or a far broader aclGroupId) and silently pre-approve an exposure nobody reviewed; a bare 'coarseAclAcknowledged': true with no binding still parses but is NOT accepted as an attestation and FAILS 'validate-config --strict'. A binding that does not match the object's effective posture is a hard config-load error - in BOTH directions, because this connector cannot know whether one Entra group is broader than another, so any change forces a fresh review rather than a guess. validate-config warns about the posture on every run either way - the attestation does NOT reduce the exposure, it only records that someone accepted it - but without a valid one 'validate-config --strict' FAILS for that object. Deliberately NOT pre-set below: the shipped config is expected to fail --strict until an operator reviews Account's ACL posture. Only valid on group/public objects; on ownerOnly either key is a config error, so a stale sign-off can never pre-approve a later widening. columnPolicies (see docs/COLUMN_POLICIES.md): optional per-object map of BDH column name -> 'drop' or 'mask'. drop = the column is never emitted (no Graph property, no content line, no title); mask = the property name and content key are kept but the value is replaced with [RESTRICTED]. Column names match case-insensitively; every key must name a column in that object's selectedFields and every value must be drop|mask, or the config fails to load - a policy that silently restricts nothing is worse than no policy. A policy on the IDENTITY column 'Id' (any casing) is likewise rejected at load: that value IS the externalItem id, the 'Url' deep link built from it, the content title fallback and the inventory/dead-letter/retry key, so a drop/mask would strip one Graph property while the value stayed indexed by three other routes and preflight would announce a restriction that is not real - remove the column from selectedFields instead, narrow the aclMode, or filter the record out in filters.json. A policy on a column whose NAME is the Graph property a DIFFERENT column maps to (selectedFields {'Id': 'RecordId', 'RecordId': 'Other'} with columnPolicies {'RecordId': 'drop'}) is rejected too: the policy applies, but preflight would report 'RecordId' as restricted while a populated property of exactly that name kept reaching the index from 'Id', so the report could not be read as true - rename the other column's property mapping, or policy that column instead. A column mapped to a property of its own name is the ordinary case and is fine, as is a collision whose colliding property is itself dropped (it never reaches the index; mask does not qualify). Dead-letter payloads need no separate policy: they are the CONVERTED item, so they inherit this gate even under DEADLETTER_PAYLOAD_MODE=full. Neither action changes the item ACL (an ACL-rewriting action is deliberately out of scope pending Ranger). Not pre-set below: which columns are restricted is a data-owner decision, and validate-config states on every run that no object restricts any column.
